market_summary: Markets are digesting an abrupt Nvidia leadership crisis (CEO Jensen Huang's resignation amid scandal, Nov 12) that triggered a wave of sell-side downgrades and pushed the stock below $4T market cap just days ahead of its Nov 17 earnings. Nasdaq/tech broadly underperformed (QQQ -1.2% Thu, -6.6% over 1m) while the Dow held up on energy/staples strength, reflecting a rotation out of richly-valued megacap tech. In Singapore, Singtel's 10% underlying profit growth and raised FY guidance drove its best day in three months, while SGX itself flagged stronger October trading volumes. SG banks (DBS/OCBC/UOB) are all down 6-9% over the past month with no fresh negative catalyst, suggesting broader regional derisking rather than company-specific issues. Tesla's Cybercab commercial launch is a notable product milestone but is offset by the simultaneous wind-down of Cybertruck production, muddying the near-term demand narrative.

picks.thesis: Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation over a personal scandal creates a leadership vacuum at the world's most important AI chip company right before its Nov 17 earnings report. Nine sell-side downgrades hit in two days (Melius, Craig-Hallum, StoneX, William Blair, Keybanc, Bernstein, Evercore, Oppenheimer, Baird), several slashing price targets by more than half, which is an unusually coordinated capitulation signal. Stock is already down 25% in a month, trading 24% below its 50-day MA and 20% below its 200-day MA with elevated relative volume (1.85x), indicating momentum and institutional repositioning are still working against it heading into a high-volatility earnings print.
picks.news: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Nov 12 following reports of affairs including one with an alleged Chinese spy; shares fell 2% on Nov 13, closing below $4T market cap for the first time since July 2025; nine analyst downgrades followed on Nov 11-12.
picks.risks: A strong Nov 17 earnings beat/guide, rapid naming of a credible permanent CEO, or a sense the scandal is unrelated to fundamentals could trigger a sharp relief rally given how oversold the stock already is and the still-bullish consensus (57 buys vs 5 sell/hold) with 96% implied upside to target.

picks.thesis: Singtel delivered 10% underlying profit growth and raised FY2027 EBIT guidance on strong subsidiary performance, triggering its best single-day gain (3%) in three months on heavy volume (3.3x normal). Analyst sentiment is overwhelmingly positive (13 buys, 2 holds, 0 sells) with 27.7% implied upside to consensus target, and the stock remains well off its highs (-21% from 52w high) despite the improving fundamental trend, leaving room to re-rate as the guidance upgrade is digested.
picks.news: Singtel H1 underlying net profit rose 10% to S$1.49B and interim dividend raised 10% to S$0.09/share (Nov 13); shares rose 3% on upgraded full-year EBIT guidance, the biggest intraday gain since mid-August (Nov 13-14).
picks.risks: Reported net profit actually fell 55% due to absence of prior-year divestment gains, so headline numbers could spook less-informed investors on follow-through days; a reversal of the regional telecom/associate tailwinds (Bharti, Telkomsel, etc.) would undercut the guidance upgrade.

picks.thesis: Tech is broadly underperforming the market (Nasdaq -0.91% vs Dow +0.1% on Nov 13) with QQQ down 6.6% over the month and sitting 10.5% below its 52-week high, below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages. The Nvidia leadership shock adds to an already fragile tech tape (GOOGL -15% 1m, MSFT -2.9% 1m), and with Nvidia earnings on Nov 17 injecting further volatility risk into a heavy index weight, near-term downside pressure on the Nasdaq-100 looks more likely than a quick recovery.
picks.news: US stocks closed mixed Nov 13 with S&P 500 -0.4% and Nasdaq -0.91% as tech and consumer discretionary lagged while energy/staples led; Nvidia fell 2% the same day on CEO fallout.
picks.risks: A strong Nvidia earnings beat or broad AI-capex reassurance from other megacaps could spark a sharp tech rally; QQQ's diversification beyond Nvidia (Apple, Amazon holding up) limits how far the index can fall purely on one stock's news.

picks.thesis: Tesla is simultaneously launching Cybercab consumer sales (a small-volume, high-hype robotaxi variant at $29,990) while winding down Cybertruck production by mid-2027, an implicit admission that its flagship new-vehicle launch of the past two years failed commercially. The stock has already rallied 7.7% over the month and 15% over three months, pricing in optimism around the Cybercab/robotaxi narrative, but analyst conviction is split (21 buy vs 21 hold) with only 5.7% implied upside, suggesting limited fresh upside unless Cybercab execution surprises materially.
picks.news: Tesla began Cybercab consumer sales/orders for December delivery (Nov 14) while confirming Cybertruck production will cease at Austin by mid-2027 due to weak sales (Nov 13).
picks.risks: Cybercab demand could exceed low expectations and reignite the robotaxi growth story; Tesla's high beta (1.74) means any broad market rally or Musk-driven news could override this thesis quickly.

picks.thesis: Singapore Exchange reported stronger October trading activity with increased securities, derivatives and ETF turnover even amid market pullbacks, a positive revenue-driver signal for a volume-sensitive business. The stock trades 19% below its 52-week high and is down nearly 19% over three months, which combined with 14.1% implied upside to consensus target and a 6/9/2 buy/hold/sell split leaves some room for a bounce if elevated trading volumes persist into November amid ongoing volatility (e.g., the Nvidia-driven tech selloff tends to boost derivatives/hedging volumes on SGX).
picks.news: SGX reported stronger October trading activity with higher securities turnover and expanding derivatives/ETF volumes as investors navigated market pullbacks (Nov 12).
picks.risks: This is a single data point about October activity (already somewhat dated) rather than a fresh catalyst, and the stock's -4.9% vs 50-day MA shows ongoing technical weakness; a calming of volatility would reduce the volume tailwind this thesis depends on.
